title: Data Pipelines
description: Batch and stream pipeline design, data contracts, idempotent reprocessing, and schema evolution — moving data reliably, not analyzing it.

levels.name: Foundation
levels.description: Can run an existing extract-load job against a named source and destination, and can point at the code or SQL that decides whether that job is a full refresh or an incremental load.

levels.name: Apprentice
levels.description: Can write a scoped batch load that lands in staging then a warehouse table, rerun it against the same source snapshot, and show that the warehouse primary-key set did not grow.

levels.name: Practitioner
levels.description: Can independently design and implement a pipeline that includes a written data contract (schema, grain, freshness, null rules), an idempotent sink, and a test that fails if a retry doubles rows.

levels.name: Journeyman
levels.description: Can diagnose a failed or drifted pipeline from run logs, offsets or watermarks, and warehouse counts; can execute a bounded backfill or replay without corrupting the current window; and can defend a schema-evolution choice (additive versus breaking) in writing.

levels.name: Mastery Evidence
levels.description: Can review another apprentice's pipeline for a missing contract clause, a non-idempotent retry path, or an unsafe backfill, name the concrete failure each would cause, and teach the batch-versus-stream and contract-versus-hope distinction to someone new to the path.
